info.title: ZeroGPU Orchestration API — ZeroClick endpoints
info.description:
OpenAPI specification for the ZeroClick-authenticated orchestration endpoints
(`/zeroclick/v1/*`).

ZeroClick sits in front of the ZeroGPU Orchestration API as the
agent-payment layer. A buying agent calls ZeroClick's hosted pay URL;
ZeroClick then proxies the request to these endpoints, signing the raw
request bytes with an HMAC in the `zc-signature` header. From this API's
perspective, a request is authenticated **only** by a valid `zc-signature`
— there is no `x-api-key` on these routes.

These endpoints mirror the standard `/v1/chat/completions`,
`/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/moderations` and `/v1/audio/*`
orchestration endpoints (same request/response bodies,
same model routing), differing only in:
  * **Authentication** — the `zc-signature` HMAC is verified over the raw
    request bytes instead of an API key.
  * **Authorization** — a ZeroClick allowance check runs before any
    billable work. It fails *open* on a transient ZeroClick outage (the
    signature has already verified), but never for a missing/invalid
    signature.
  * **Metering** — actual usage is reported back to ZeroClick via the
    `zc-usage` response header on success: input/output tokens for the
    text endpoints, audio seconds for the audio endpoints. Stripe metering is intentionally
    bypassed; ZeroClick is the sole biller.

post.description:
OpenAI-style Chat Completions endpoint, authenticated by verifying the
`zc-signature` HMAC over the raw request bytes. The request is routed by
`model` using model metadata, and the same orchestration as
`/v1/chat/completions` runs behind it.

On success, actual token usage is settled with ZeroClick and reported
via the `zc-usage` response header.

200.description: OpenAI Chat Completions response. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

post.description:
OpenAI-style Responses endpoint, authenticated by verifying the
`zc-signature` HMAC over the raw request bytes. The request is routed by
`model` using model metadata, and the same orchestration as
`/v1/responses` runs behind it.

On success, actual token usage is settled with ZeroClick and reported
via the `zc-usage` response header.

200.description: OpenAI Responses `response` object. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

post.description:
OpenAI-style Embeddings endpoint. Billed on input tokens only; `zc-usage`
reports the `prompt_tokens` from the response's `usage`.

Authenticated by verifying the `zc-signature` HMAC over the raw
request bytes; the same orchestration as `/v1/embeddings` runs behind it.

example.input: ZeroGPU runs high-volume inference tasks on small models at the edge.

200.description: OpenAI embeddings list. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

post.description:
OpenAI-style Moderations endpoint. `model` may be omitted (the configured
moderation model is used) or given as an OpenAI id such as
`omni-moderation-latest`, which is mapped to it. `zc-usage` reports the
input and output tokens from the response's `usage`.

Authenticated by verifying the `zc-signature` HMAC over the raw
request bytes; the same orchestration as `/v1/moderations` runs behind it.

example.input: I am so angry at this person that I want to hurt them. They are worthless and should be scared of what I might do next.

200.description: OpenAI moderations envelope. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

post.description:
OpenAI-style speech-to-text in the source language. The body is streamed upstream unread, so the model is the configured `whisper-tiny`
rather than one read from the request. Billed per audio second: the allowance
check asks for the 1-second floor, and `zc-usage` reports
`max(1, ceil(x-audio-duration-seconds))` audio seconds on success.

Authenticated by verifying the `zc-signature` HMAC over the raw
request bytes; the same orchestration as `/v1/audio/transcriptions` runs behind it.

200.description: The transcript, in the requested `response_format`. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

value.text: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

text/plain.example: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

413.description: File over 25 MB (`file_too_large`) or audio too long (`audio_too_long`)

post.description:
OpenAI-style speech-to-text that always returns English. The body is streamed upstream unread, so the model is the configured `whisper-tiny`
rather than one read from the request. Billed per audio second: the allowance
check asks for the 1-second floor, and `zc-usage` reports
`max(1, ceil(x-audio-duration-seconds))` audio seconds on success.

Authenticated by verifying the `zc-signature` HMAC over the raw
request bytes; the same orchestration as `/v1/audio/translations` runs behind it.

200.description: The English transcript, in the requested `response_format`. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

413.description: File over 25 MB (`file_too_large`) or audio too long (`audio_too_long`)

post.description:
Text-to-speech, with optional voice cloning from a `voice_sample` sent as
multipart. The body is streamed upstream unread, so the model is the configured `chatterbox-nano`
rather than one read from the request. Billed per audio second: the allowance
check asks for the 1-second floor, and `zc-usage` reports
`max(1, ceil(x-audio-duration-seconds))` audio seconds on success.

Authenticated by verifying the `zc-signature` HMAC over the raw
request bytes; the same orchestration as `/v1/audio/speech` runs behind it.

example.input: Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?
Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?

200.description: The audio file, with a content type matching `response_format`. Includes the `zc-usage` header settling actual usage with ZeroClick.

413.description: Reference clip over 10 MB (`voice_sample_too_large`) or over 30 seconds (`voice_sample_too_long`)

422.description: Reference clip could not be used to clone a voice (`voice_conditioning_failed`), no audio was produced (`empty_audio`), or the format cannot be encoded (`response_format_unavailable`)

ZeroClickSignature.name: zc-signature
ZeroClickSignature.description:
HMAC signature minted by ZeroClick over the raw request bytes, of the
form `t=<unix-seconds>,kid=<key-id>,v1=<hex-hmac>`. Verified by the
`@zeroclickai/sellers` SDK against the seller's signing secret keyed by
`kid`. A missing or invalid signature is rejected with `401`
`invalid_zeroclick_signature`; this is never failed open.

ZcRequestId.name: zc-request-id
ZcRequestId.description: ZeroClick request id, echoed in logs for correlation. Set by ZeroClick when it proxies the request.

ZcAgentId.name: zc-agent-id
ZcAgentId.description: Identifier of the buying agent. Used to partition logs/analytics by agent; becomes the synthesized caller identity.

ZcUsage.description:
Usage report settled with ZeroClick, present on `200` responses. Encodes
the actual usage metered against the request's ZeroClick service slug
(the kebab-cased model id, e.g. `lfm2-5-1-2b-instruct`): `input_tokens`
and `output_tokens` for chat completions, responses and moderations,
`input_tokens` only for embeddings, and `audio_seconds` for the audio
endpoints.

XRequestId.description: Correlation id for this request, present on every response.

XInferenceType.description: Where inference executed (e.g. `cloud` or an on-device route). Absent when inference ran neither on the edge nor in the cloud.

XAudioDurationSeconds.description: Audio length in seconds: the uploaded audio for a transcription or translation, the generated audio for speech. ZeroClick is billed `max(1, ceil(x-audio-duration-seconds))` audio seconds.

ZeroClickUnauthorized.description:
The `zc-signature` was missing or invalid, or ZeroClick is not configured
for this environment. Unsigned/unverifiable traffic is treated as
unauthenticated.

PaymentRequired.description:
The ZeroClick allowance check denied the request (e.g. insufficient
allowance or a stale signature timestamp). Body follows ZeroClick's
`payment_required` schema as returned by the SDK.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request — malformed JSON, or a missing/invalid required field such as `model` or `messages`.

ContextLengthExceeded.description: Input token count exceeds the resolved model's `max_tokens` and the model is configured to error rather than truncate.

error.message: Input exceeds max_tokens (4096) for model: LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct

ResponsesBadRequest.description: Invalid request — malformed JSON, or a missing/invalid required field such as `model` or `input`. Errors use the Responses error envelope.

ResponsesContextLengthExceeded.description: Input token count exceeds the resolved model's `max_tokens` and the model is configured to error rather than truncate. Returned in the Responses error envelope.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit reached. Limits are counted per ZeroClick agent, so one busy agent does not throttle the others. Wait at least `Retry-After` seconds, then retry.

ModerationsBadRequest.description: Invalid request — malformed JSON, or a missing/invalid `input`.

error.message: We could not parse the JSON body of your request. (HINT: This likely means you are not using your HTTP library correctly. The ZeroGPU API expects a JSON payload, but what was sent was not valid JSON.)

AudioBadRequest.description: Bad request — a body that is not the expected content type, or an invalid or missing field.

ModelUnavailable.description: Model warming up (`model_unavailable`) or every slot busy (`server_busy`). Retry with backoff.

model.description: Model id; routes the request via model metadata. Kebab-cased into a ZeroClick service slug for metering.

categories.description: Candidate labels for text-classification models. May also be supplied via a system-role message.

multilingual.description: Forwarded to the IAB cloud inference API only when the resolved model supports it.

metadata.description:
Task-specific options. For GLiNER models this carries `usecase`,
`schema`, `labels`, `threshold`, `mask`, and `replacement_char`. For
moderation, `threshold`; for signal-extract, `max_keywords`.

role.description: A `developer` role is normalized to `system`; unrecognized roles are treated as `user`.

ChatCompletionResponse.description: OpenAI Chat Completions response. For classification models, `choices[0].message.content` is a JSON-stringified classification result.

input.description: Prompt text. Combined with `instructions` (as a system message) to form the model input.

instructions.description: System-style instructions prepended to the input. Classification models may pass comma-separated or bracketed candidate labels here.

metadata.description: Up to 16 string key/value pairs echoed back in the response envelope. Also carries GLiNER usecase options (`usecase`, `schema`, `labels`, `threshold`, `mask`, `replacement_char`), which are consumed and not necessarily echoed.

type.description: Output format. `text` is supported; `json` is currently rejected.

ResponsesResponse.description: OpenAI Responses `response` object. On error, `status` is `failed` and `error` is populated.

ResponsesError.description:
Error attached to a Responses envelope. OpenAI's ResponseError carries
`code` and `message`; `type` and `param` are also emitted by some error
sites on this endpoint.

ZeroClickSignatureError.description: Returned when the `zc-signature` is missing/invalid or ZeroClick is unconfigured.

PaymentRequiredError.description: ZeroClick `payment_required` denial body, produced by the `@zeroclickai/sellers` SDK.

model.description: Embedding model to use. Embedding models are routable only on this endpoint.

input.description: Text to embed. A single string, or an array of strings (one vector per element). Inputs are truncated at the model's max token length.

index.description: Position of the input this vector was produced from.

embedding.description: The embedding vector. 384 dimensions for both models.

EmbeddingUsage.description: Embeddings are billed on input tokens only; there are no output tokens.

model.description: Moderation model to use. Defaults to the configured moderation model; OpenAI ids (`omni-moderation-latest`, `text-moderation-stable`) are accepted and mapped to it.

input.description: Text to classify. A single string, an array of strings (one result per element), or an array of content parts (`{ "type": "text", "text": "..." }`) forming one multi-modal input.

ModerationResponse.description: OpenAI-compatible moderations envelope. One `results` entry per input.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation request.

results.description: Moderation verdicts, one per input (a string input yields a single-element array).

ModerationResult.description: A single entry of the `results` array — the verdict for one input.

flagged.description: True when the model flagged the input in one or more categories.

ModerationCategories.description: Per-category boolean verdicts. All 13 categories are always present, in OpenAI's order.

harassment.description: Content that expresses, incites, or promotes harassing language towards any target.

harassment/threatening.description: Harassment that also includes violence or serious harm towards any target.

hate.description: Content that expresses, incites, or promotes hate based on a protected attribute.

hate/threatening.description: Hateful content that also includes violence or serious harm towards a protected group.

illicit.description: Content that gives advice or instruction on how to commit a wrongdoing.

illicit/violent.description: Illicit content that also references violence or procuring a weapon.

self-harm.description: Content that promotes, encourages, or depicts acts of self-harm.

self-harm/intent.description: Content where the speaker expresses that they are engaging or intend to engage in self-harm.

self-harm/instructions.description: Content that provides instructions or advice on how to commit acts of self-harm.

sexual.description: Content meant to arouse sexual excitement or that promotes sexual services.

sexual/minors.description: Sexual content that includes an individual under 18 years old.

violence.description: Content that depicts death, violence, or physical injury.

violence/graphic.description: Content that depicts death, violence, or physical injury in graphic detail.

ModerationCategoryScores.description: Per-category confidence scores in [0, 1]. All 13 categories are always present, in OpenAI's order.

ModerationAppliedInputTypes.description: Which input modality triggered each category. This is a text-only model, so every category maps to ["text"].

language.description: ISO-639-1 code, such as `en`. Detected automatically when omitted.

prompt.description: Text to guide spelling and style, such as names or jargon.

CreateSpeechRequest.description: JSON body, as the OpenAI SDKs send it. Use `multipart/form-data` to attach a `voice_sample`.

input.example: Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?
input.description: The text to speak. Inline tags such as `[laugh]` and `[cough]` add paralinguistic cues.

voice.description: OpenAI voice names are accepted and all map to the built-in voice.

response_format.description: `pcm` is raw 16-bit little-endian mono at 24 kHz.

CreateSpeechMultipartRequest.description: Multipart form, required for voice cloning.

input.example: Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?
input.description: The text to speak. Inline tags such as `[laugh]` and `[cough]` add paralinguistic cues.

voice.description: OpenAI voice names are accepted and all map to the built-in voice.

response_format.description: `pcm` is raw 16-bit little-endian mono at 24 kHz.

voice_sample.description: Reference clip to clone a voice from. Overrides `voice`. Not stored.

file.description: The audio file to translate into English.

prompt.description: Text to guide spelling and style, such as names or jargon.

CreateTranslationRequest.description: Same form as a transcription, without `language`: the transcript is always English. Sending `language` returns `400`.
